degree_context.program: Computer Science, B.S. - Theory and Application Track
degree_context.variant: Theory and Application is the canonical broad-computing path; Cybersecurity and Information Technology are separately published required track variants
degree_context.academic_unit: Department of Computer and Information Sciences

upper_division.reason: The reviewed current catalog and academic-regulation sources state no aggregate upper-division-credit minimum; track-specific upper-level requirements remain explicit in the curriculum.

residency.rule: At least six qualifying full-time semesters and at least 50 percent of the academic program must be completed at VMI; the published transfer guidance imposes a 75-percent in-residence rule on cadets entering without advanced-standing credit.

modeling_notes: The live 2025-2026 academic catalog publishes three materially different Computer Science B.S. tracks. Their trees must remain separate rather than being flattened into one menu.
VMI's Core, ROTC, leadership, human-performance, writing-intensive, capstone, GPA, and residence rules are graduation requirements and must be composed with the selected track.
Catalog curriculum tables are authoritative requirement allocations. Marketing or advising schedules are not substituted for them.

college.note: VMI is a single undergraduate institute; the Computer and Information Sciences department is the academic owner and there is no intervening college requirement layer.
